findings.finding: Undated recalls can become negatives; incidence unverified
findings.rationale: The documents describe missing recall linkage, date boundaries and parse checks, but do not state that an undated linked recall can leave a clearance negative. A date-parse check is not disclosure of this label consequence.

evidence.value: The outcome is linked only through the 510(k) number: 20,792 of 59,705 device recall product records carry no k_number and are invisible, so the label is a lower bound on true recall incidence for cleared devices.
event_date_initiated is the firm's action date, not FDA's classification date, so a recall initiated near the end of a window but classified later can sit at the boundary.

Two plain HTTPS downloads, no account or key, both resolved in one pass because signed or dated product URLs expire: https://download.open.fda.gov/device/510k/device-510k-0001-of-0001.json.zip and https://download.open.fda.gov/device/recall/device-recall-0001-of-0001.json.zip. fetch(url, cache, name) keeps the local file plus its URL and SHA256. Each archive holds one UTF-8 JSON member containing a meta envelope and a results array; locate the results array by finding the quoted results key whose value is an array (the meta block also carries a results key, but its value is an object), then decode one record at a time with json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode over a 1 MB chunk buffer. Read last_updated from the recall meta head for the snapshot date. Build the clearance table from k_number, decision_date, date_received, decision_code, clearance_type, advisory_committee, product_code, third_party_flag, applicant, country_code and openfda.device_class; index the recall table by exploded k_numbers with event_date_initiated; label a clearance positive when any recall event date for that k_number falls between decision_date and decision_date plus 1826 days.

findings.rationale: Construction notes describe collapsing resolved episodes but omit the choice of the earliest date when dates differ. Neither document states the resulting possibility that an active episode passes the exclusion.

evidence.value: Repair scope: the saved builder was rejected before execution with the message that the source access recipe must be nonempty text, so this repair supplies a concrete nonempty access recipe and adds no change to the frozen question, population, label, features or split windows. Code defects fixed while preserving behaviour: (1) the archive reader ended with a bare raise that could only ever surface a RuntimeError without evidence, and it now raises an AssertionError naming the archive member and the decoding error; (2) the conservative HPV resolution collapse was reimplemented in vectorised form but keeps exactly the previous rule, so a resolution date is used only when every row of a facility and day-zero group carries one, and otherwise the episode stays open; (3) exclusion counts for active HPV, same-day day-zero and another full evaluation in the prior 365 days are now recorded before the filters run, so the funnel check reports how many rows each frozen rule removed instead of re-reporting zero on rows that were already filtered, and the post-filter checks still assert zero; (4) field names are resolved from the observed archived header with a small candidate list per table, and any resolution failure raises with the archive member name, the missing candidate names and the observed headers bounded to 4000 characters, so a header mismatch is diagnosable rather than silent. Honest limitations retained: the supplied research names the stack-test and Title V certification tables but not their exact date columns, so those builders probe documented candidate names in a fixed order and fail with header evidence instead of silently guessing; the facilities table is expected to expose STATE, EPA_REGION, FACILITY_TYPE_CODE, SIC_CODES, NAICS_CODES and AIR_POLLUTANT_CLASS_CODE, with STATE_CODE and AIR_POLLUTANT_CLASS accepted only as naming variants, and this expectation is an assumption rather than a verified data dictionary entry. Title V deviation interpretation is now evidence-based rather than an abort on the entire table: confirmed Yes values count as reported deviations, No values count as none, and any other value is recorded in that check and treated as no confirmed deviation, so the build state that a row-level flag is unconfirmed rather than silently calling it a deviation. No feature is derived from labels, no group rates or target encodings are shipped, no threshold is fitted on eval or holdout, and unknown HPV outcomes are never turned into negative labels because the population requires a fully observed 365-day horizon before the snapshot boundary. Program and pollutant counts remain current-snapshot membership counts, and days-since and penalty features stay blank rather than zero when the source supplies no value; a penalty of zero is written only when there were no formal actions at all. No execution against the live archive was possible in this write-only phase, so table row counts, population funnel counts, per-split positives and feature coverage are computed from the constructed frame and will surface as check failures with their actual values if the current snapshot differs from the documented semantics; the 2026-11-07 extract boundary comes from the publisher index and is not inferred from holdout rows. references are unchanged because the prior HPV episode count remains the available persistence score column with increasing risk direction.

FCE activity rows from ICIS-AIR_FCES_PCES.csv with COMP_MONITOR_TYPE_CODE in {FOO, FFO}; ACTUAL_END_DATE in a frozen half-open split window; at least one ICIS-AIR_PROGRAMS.csv row for the facility; no active HPV episode at t, meaning HPV_DAYZERO_DATE <= t and HPV_RESOLVED_DATE is null or > t; no HPV day-zero equal to t; no other full evaluation at the same facility with ACTUAL_END_DATE in [t-365 days, t); and t+365 days on or before 2026-11-07. Duplicate FCE activity rows and same-facility same-day full evaluations are collapsed deterministically.

findings.rationale: The split policy explicitly requires the prior period to end before the split starts. The documents do not explain its consequence: only first post-boundary periods survive and some monitoring cycles disappear from scoring.

evidence.value: Chronological on target SAMPLING_START_DATE with fixed half-open windows train 1995-01-01 to 2014-01-01, eval 2014-01-01 to 2019-01-01 and holdout 2019-01-01 to 2024-01-01. For eval and holdout the prior period SAMPLING_END_DATE must be before the split start; train is the earliest split and retains only prior dates before each target period. No shuffling. Each system contributes at most one row per target period after latest-reported de-duplication. The primacy-agency floor is computed from pairs whose prior period ended before 2014-01-01 and uses no labels.

Community water systems in the EPA ECHO SDWA national download whose PWS_TYPE_CODE field is CWS and that have at least two PB90 lead 90th-percentile summary records, where the target PB90 period starts strictly after the prior PB90 period end and no more than four years later, with target period start on or before 2023-12-31. No filter on current PWS_ACTIVITY_CODE. Primacy agencies with fewer than 20 eligible pairs whose prior period ended before 2014-01-01 are excluded from all splits; this floor uses training-era feature dates only.
